Moldavia proper is the 1595 outline; the rest belongs to Wallachia and Transylvania.

70,620 km2; two cells moved on the lower Dniester (28.6-28.8 E, 46.3 N). The 1791-1792 Treaty of Jassy is not on the pages opened (unverified: page budget); Kucuk Kaynarca (1774) says nothing about Moldavia's frontier.

42,009 km2: 28,589 km2 (113 cells) less than 1806. The Bucharest page: 'the Budjak and the eastern half of the Principality of Moldavia, between Prut and Dniester Rivers' (45,630 km2, which includes the Budjak and Khotyn that were already under direct Ottoman rule); 70,620 less 28,589 is the Prut-bounded Moldavia.
42,009 km2; Russian protectorate 1829-1856 (infobox), occupation 1828-1834 bridged in the ledger. Same outline as 1814.
42,009 km2; unchanged. Russian protectorate, no territorial event on the pages.
42,009 km2; unchanged to 1848.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1856 to February 1859 (Treaty of Paris 30 March 1856; union 5 February 1859)

keyframe_review.note: 54,293 km2: 11,891 km2 (47 cells, 28.1-30.1 E, 45.0-46.4 N) more than 1848, southern Bessarabia: Russia 'had to return to Moldavia' the part it 'had annexed in 1812' at the Danube mouth (Treaty of Paris, 30 March 1856). Years only: the shape holds from 1856 and to the union of 5 February 1859.

correction.text: the 1768 outline, under Russian occupation until the peace of 21 July 1774 and with Bukovina occupied by the Habsburgs from October 1774

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 1769-1774. Moldavia was an Ottoman principality under Russian occupation; the Kucuk Kaynarca page says 'Russia returned Wallachia and Moldavia to Ottoman control' (21 July 1774) and the Bukovina page that the peace 'ended the Russian occupation of Moldavia'. No page opened dates its start (confidence 1), and none moves the border before Habsburg troops 'captured the region in October 1774' (Bukovina).

correction.text: the 1806 outline, under Russian occupation until the Treaty of Bucharest of 28 May 1812 (occupation start undated: confidence 1)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 1807-1813. The Russo-Turkish War ran 1806-1812 ('Russians occupied Bucharest during the war', no dates); Moldavia stays the 1806 outline until the cession of 28 May 1812.

correction.text: the western half of Moldavia up to the Prut, from the cession of 28 May 1812

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1814 outline applies from the Treaty of Bucharest (signed 28 May 1812, ratified 5 July) rather than 1814: 'the Budjak and the eastern half of the Principality of Moldavia, between Prut and Dniester' went to Russia.

correction.text: the 1827 outline, under Russian occupation and from 1829 a Russian protectorate

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 1828-1833. Russo-Turkish War 1828-1829; 'Russian protectorate (1829-1856)' (infobox); the page does not date the end of the occupation (Cliopatria's shape returns in 1834).

correction.text: the 1848 outline, under Russian occupation from 1853 and the Russian protectorate until the Treaty of Paris of 30 March 1856

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 1849-1856. The Treaty of Paris page: the Crimean War began on 23 October 1853 'after Russian troops occupied the Danubian Principalities'; the principalities were 'recognized as quasi-independent states under Ottoman suzerainty' in 1856. The page does not date the evacuation or mention the Austrian occupation.

region.text: the Baia region of Suceava County, Bogdan's first seat before Siret

ledger.note: 1359: Bogdan of Cuhea takes Moldavia from Hungary. Bogdan 'crossed the Carpathians in 1359, took control of Moldavia' and wrested it from Hungary; the infobox dates the Moldavian mark to 1346 (Dragos, 1346-1353, 'vassal to Hungary'). The page gives the Baia region, not a boundary.

region.text: Cetatea Alba on the Dniester estuary and the Black Sea coast of the Budjak

ledger.note: 1392: Roman I takes Cetatea Alba. 'His brother Roman I conquered the Hungarian-ruled Cetatea Alba in 1392, giving Moldavia an outlet to the Black Sea' (Moldavia page); the same page has Prince Petru (before 1392, undated) 'also expanded his rule southwards to the Danube Delta'. The fortress was Hungarian-ruled, hence the counterpart; the page names no holder for the Budjak steppe behind it. Cliopatria draws the Budjak as Moldavian from 1363. [Reviewer eu-18-e: counterpart changed from 'nobody' and quote completed after reading the page.]
1448: Peter III hands Chilia to Hungary. 'Peter III had handed Chilia, a Danube port, to Hungary in 1448.' One fortress; the outline is unchanged.
1465: Stephen the Great retakes Chilia. He besieged it in 1462 'and was wounded, then retook it in 1465' ('Stephen again laid siege to Chilia on 24 January 1465').
1465: Stephen regains Hotin from Poland. He 'regained the Dniester fortress of Hotin from Poland in 1465 or earlier'.

14-15 July 1484: Bayezid II takes Chilia. 'Bayezid invaded Moldavia and captured Chilia on 14 or 15 July 1484.' Stephen had to 'surrender Chilia and Cetatea Alba ... to the Ottomans in 1484' (Moldavia page).

region.text: Cetatea Alba (Akkerman) and the Budjak coast

ledger.note: 3 August 1484: Cetatea Alba falls. 'His vassal, Menli I Giray, also broke into Moldavia and seized Cetatea Alba on 3 August'; the Bessarabia page says the Ottoman Empire 'invaded and captured Chilia and Cetatea Alba' and annexed the southern shoreline. Counterpart set to the suzerain, the Ottomans; Cliopatria dates the loss 1487.

region.text: Pokuttia between the Dniester and the Cheremosh, around Kolomyia

ledger.note: 1490: Stephen occupies Pokuttia. 'In 1490, Stephen occupied Pokuttia', detaching it from Poland (Obertyn page). Cliopatria's shape holds only 3 cells of it.

22 August 1531: Moldavia loses Pokuttia at Obertyn. 'The battle ended with a Polish victory and the reconquest of Pokutia' (the Moldavia page: 'lost by Moldavia in the Battle of Obertyn (1531)'); a further attempt failed in 1538.

region.text: Bessarabian land in the south as far as Tighina (Bender)

ledger.note: 1538: the Ottomans annex the south of Bessarabia as far as Tighina. 'In 1538 the Ottomans annexed more Bessarabian land in the south as far as Tighina'; 'central and northern Bessarabia stayed part of Moldavia'. The region is the researcher's reading (Bender/Tighina county).

region.text: Moldavia proper, entered by Michael the Brave's troops

ledger.note: 14 April 1600: Michael the Brave invades Moldavia. 'On 14 April 1600 Michael's troops entered Moldavia on multiple routes' and he 'reached the capital of Iasi on 6 May', deposing Ieremia Movila; he 'changed his seal to represent his personal union of Wallachia, Moldavia, and Transylvania'.

September 1600: the Poles drive the Wallachians out. 'A Polish army led by Jan Zamoyski drove the Wallachians from Moldavia', restoring Ieremia Movila; the infobox ends Michael's Moldavian reign in September 1600 (the page gives no day).

1769: the Russians in Moldavia. No page opened dates the start of the Russian occupation in the 1768-1774 war; the Moldavia page mentions an 'extensive census' of 1769-1774 under it, and the Kucuk Kaynarca page says it was handed back in 1774, so 1769 is a bridge.

21 July 1774: Russia returns Moldavia to the Ottomans. Kucuk Kaynarca, 'signed on 21 July [O.S. 10 July] 1774': 'Russia returned Wallachia and Moldavia to Ottoman control' with a right to intervene 'in case of Ottoman misrule'; the Bukovina page: the peace of 21 July 1774 'ended the Russian occupation of Moldavia'.

region.text: Bukovina, the northwestern part of Moldavia

ledger.note: October 1774: Habsburg troops occupy Bukovina. 'The Habsburg Monarchy captured the region in October 1774', after the Russo-Ottoman peace.
7 May 1775: the occupation becomes a cession (Convention of Pera).

7 May 1775: Moldavia loses Bukovina. 'In 1775, Moldavia lost to the Habsburg Empire its northwestern part, which became known as Bukovina' (Moldavia page); the Austro-Ottoman Convention of Pera, signed 7 May 1775, 'officially ceded' it; the border convention of 2 July 1776 gave back 59 villages and kept 278.
1806: the Russians in Moldavia. The Bucharest page has the Russo-Turkish War of 1806-1812 and Russian troops in Bucharest 'during the war' without dates; 1806 is the war's first year, a bridge.

region.text: 'the Budjak and the eastern half of the Principality of Moldavia, between Prut and Dniester Rivers', 45,630 km2 with the Budjak

ledger.note: 28 May 1812: Moldavia loses everything east of the Prut. The Treaty of Bucharest, 'signed on 28 May 1812 ... and ratified on 5 July 1812', gave Russia 'the Budjak and the eastern half of the Principality of Moldavia'; Bessarabia page: 'the Ottoman Empire ceded the land between the Pruth and the Dniester'.
1812: Russian troops leave western Moldavia. The Bucharest page says nothing of a withdrawal; the treaty year is a bridge (Cliopatria's gap ends in 1813).

1828: the Russians in Moldavia again. The page gives 'the Russo-Turkish War 1828-1829' and a 'Russian protectorate (1829-1856)'; the start of the occupation is not dated (bridge from the war's first year).
1834: the Russian occupation ends. The page does not mention 1834; Cliopatria's shape returns in 1834, which is the only evidence (bridge).

1853: Russian troops in the Danubian Principalities. The Crimean War began on 23 October 1853 'after Russian troops occupied the Danubian Principalities'; the page does not give the occupation's own date, so the year is the war's.

1856: no Russian influence left. The Treaty of Paris says Russia 'lost any claim to influence the Danubian principalities'; the page does not date the evacuation, so the treaty is the upper bound (bridge).

region.text: the part of southern Bessarabia at the Danube mouth that Russia 'had annexed in 1812' (Cahul, Bolgrad, Ismail), about 11,900 km2 in Cliopatria

ledger.note: 30 March 1856: southern Bessarabia returns to Moldavia. Treaty of Paris: Russia 'had to return to Moldavia' the part it had annexed in 1812 'at the mouth of the Danube in southern Bessarabia', so that Russia 'lost access to the Danube river' (Bessarabia page). The page does not name Cahul, Bolgrad or Ismail; Cliopatria draws the land from 1857.

region.text: Moldavia, in the United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia

ledger.note: 5 February 1859: Moldavia and Wallachia unite. Alexandru Ioan Cuza was elected prince in Iasi on 17 January [5 January O.S.] 1859 and 'also elected in Wallachia on February 5 (January 24)', the day the article treats as unification; the infobox's 'Union with Wallachia: 5 February [24 January O.S.] 1862' is the formal United Principalities.

wars.name: Hungarian invasion of Moldavia (Battle of Baia)
wars.outcome: Matthias Corvinus invaded and took Baia, Bacau, Roman and Targu Neamt; Stephen 'launched a crushing defeat on the invaders in the Battle of Baia on 15 December' (year implied by context).

wars.name: Ottoman-Moldavian war (Vaslui and Valea Alba)
wars.outcome: Stephen beat Hadim Suleiman Pasha at Podul Inalt near Vaslui on 10 January 1475 and lost to the sultan at Valea Alba (Razboieni) on 26 July 1476; no border moved; Stephen stopped the tribute in 1473 and resumed it in 1486.

wars.name: Ottoman and Crimean Tatar invasion of 1484

zones.text: Chilia and Cetatea Alba, the Budjak ports

wars.outcome: Chilia fell on 14-15 July and Cetatea Alba on 3 August 1484 to Bayezid II and his vassal Menli I Giray; Moldavian forces burned both ports in 1500.

wars.name: Polish invasion of 1497 (Cosmin Forest)
wars.outcome: The Polish army that crossed the Dniester in August 1497 was routed on 25-26 October in the Cosmin forest; the treaty ratified at Harlau in 1499 'put an end to Polish suzerainty over Moldavia'.

wars.name: Battle of Obertyn (Polish-Moldavian war over Pokuttia)
wars.outcome: Moldavian campaigns in Pokuttia 1529-1530; Polish victory under Jan Tarnowski at Obertyn on 22 August 1531 and reconquest of Pokuttia; another Moldavian attempt failed in 1538.

wars.name: Michael the Brave's conquest of Moldavia
wars.outcome: Michael entered Moldavia on 14 April 1600, reached Iasi on 6 May and ruled it until September; Jan Zamoyski's Polish army drove the Wallachians out and restored Ieremia Movila.
wars.note: He took Transylvania after Selimbar (18 October 1599) and lost it in September 1600 (infobox).

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774)
wars.outcome: Kucuk Kaynarca, 21 July 1774: Russia returned Moldavia and Wallachia to the Ottomans with a right of intervention; the Habsburgs occupied Bukovina in October 1774 and obtained it on 7 May 1775.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)

zones.text: the eastern half of Moldavia and the Budjak

wars.outcome: Treaty of Bucharest, 28 May 1812: Russia obtained the Budjak and the eastern half of Moldavia between the Prut and the Dniester (45,630 km2).

wars.name: Crimean War (Danubian Principalities)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Paris, 30 March 1856: Russia returned the southern Bessarabian strip to Moldavia; the principalities became 'quasi-independent states under Ottoman suzerainty' and Russia lost all claim to influence over them.

certainty.note: Carpathian, Dniester and steppe frontiers are approximate; the Polish frontier is stated by treaty only in 1459 and 1499 without lines.
Bukovina line by the convention of 2 July 1776; the Prut line from the Treaty of Bucharest (1812); the Paris line of 1856. The Dniester and Khotyn frontier before 1812 stays approximate.

notes:
Pages opened: nine of nine allowed (Moldavia, Stephen the Great, Michael the Brave, Bukovina, Bessarabia, Treaty of Kucuk Kaynarca, Treaty of Bucharest 1812, Treaty of Paris 1856, Battle of Obertyn). The Moldavia infobox has no area; the body gives 94,862 km2 for the late 15th century (Cliopatria 98,334-99,177 in 1450-1486, ratio 1.04-1.05; 82,069 after 1484, ratio 0.87).
Start: 1359 (Bogdan) rather than the infobox's 1346 'Moldavian mark', a Hungarian vassal polity; Cliopatria begins 1363. End: February 1859 (Cuza elected at Bucharest on 5 February), not 1862 (infobox) or Cliopatria's 1858.
Cliopatria rows to correct: the 1600-1601 shape is Michael the Brave's whole union drawn as Moldavia (256,733 km2): Moldavia proper is the 1595 outline (adjust); the Budjak is drawn Moldavian from 1363 but the page gives Cetatea Alba to Roman I in 1392 (adjust 1363, 1375, 1385); Cliopatria's gaps 1769-1774, 1791, 1807-1813, 1828-1833, 1849-1856 are Russian occupations or empty years: new keyframes carry the outline, events carry the occupations (start dates at confidence 1 where no page dates them).
Not drawn here because they belong to the suzerain: Hungarian suzerainty of the Moldavian mark (1346-1359), Polish suzerainty (Petru II became 'a vassal of Wladyslaw II on September 26, 1387'; 4 April 1459 treaty with Casimir IV; Colomea 12 September 1485; ended by the treaty ratified at Harlau in 1499), Ottoman tribute from Petru Aron (1451-) and 'Ottoman vassal (1498-1572; 1574-1600; 1618-1859)', 'Polish vassal (1601-1618)' and 'Russian protectorate (1829-1856)', 'International protectorate (1856-1859)' (all infobox). kingdom-of-poland/house-of-jagiellon, ottoman-empire (me-10), polish-lithuanian-commonwealth and russian-empire should carry vassal events with counterpart principality-of-moldavia; the Ottoman dossier's 1878 vassal_end rows naming Moldavia need re-pointing (eu-18-g note).
Pages silent on: the 1375-1384 and 1402-1430 Dniester strip, the Khotyn tip's in-and-out (Khotyn was under direct Ottoman rule before 1812 per the Bessarabia page, undated), the 1792 Treaty of Jassy, the Russian occupation 1828-1834 dates, the Austrian occupation 1854-1857, the 1791 and the 1849-1856 empty years' outline, who held Cetatea Alba before 1392. Counterparts needing a Moldavia-side entry elsewhere: kingdom-of-hungary (Chilia 1448 and 1465, 1359), house-of-jagiellon (Hotin 1465, Pokuttia 1490 and 1531), ottoman-empire (1484, 1538), principality-of-wallachia (April-September 1600 occupation), habsburg-monarchy (Bukovina October 1774, 7 May 1775), russian-empire (1812, 1856, occupations), united-principalities-of-moldavia-and-wallachia (1859).
Gazetteer names used that the gazetteer lacks: region 'Pokuttya' (Pokuttia, Kolomyia-Sniatyn-Horodenka, south-east of Ivano-Frankivsk oblast); places Baia (Suceava County), Siret, Chilia/Kiliia, Hotin/Khotyn, Cetatea Alba/Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi (used here as coordinates or the Budjak region).
